assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) reframed cell compartmentalization in physical-chemical terms: thermodynamics of demixing, multivalent interactions, and non-equilibrium material states. It is conceptually original and connects directly to the soft-matter and colloid physical chemistry I know well.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the founding observation of liquid-like P granules and the physical framing; Rosen supplied the multivalent-protein phase-diagram model system. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded theory and biophysics, so credit is broad and the three-person limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Over a decade of independent confirmation across many labs, with a large literature and strong follow-on impact. Timing looks ripe, though the field is still debating which condensates are functionally relevant in vivo.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance of many reported condensates versus in vitro droplets remains contested.
Allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are an application of lipid self-assembly and membrane physical chemistry that enabled siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines at global scale. The impact is exceptional and the underlying lipid phase behavior and pKa-dependent fusogenicity is real chemistry, not only engineering.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) developed the early ionizable-lipid entrapment and LNP formulation; Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan contributed lipids and translation. Allocation relative to the 2023 Medicine prize and across academic and industry contributors is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at enormous scale since 2018 and 2020. Recognition is timely, but the Medicine prize in 2023 for mRNA modifications may make the Committee cautious about overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize.
Fair split between the Vancouver group and Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan; my recollection of detailed priority is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and excited-state reactivity under mild conditions and is now a routine tool in synthesis and pharmaceutical chemistry. The concept is clear, broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently established the synthetic use of Ru/Ir and organic photocatalysts around 2008-2012; MacMillan (already a laureate), König, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi have strong claims too. Credit is genuinely shared.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely adopted for over a decade. Recognition is timely, although the crowded credit makes a clean configuration hard.
uncertainties: MacMillan, a 2021 laureate, would complicate a configuration that omits him.
Priority between Yoon, Stephenson and the earlier work of Fukuzumi and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale mass-spectrometry proteomics transformed biology by allowing systematic identification and quantification of proteins and modifications. Its impact is foundational even if it is more analytical than conceptual.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the most commonly identified architects (high-resolution MS-based proteomics, SRM/SWATH-style quantification, shotgun MudPIT). Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also strong, so a three-person prize leaves out serious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly used for two decades; the 2002 prize already recognized ESI and MALDI, so this would be a follow-on analytical recognition.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of ionization methods in 2002.
Ordering and selection among six credited names is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite solar cells reached silicon-competitive efficiencies in about a decade, a striking materials-chemistry advance with large energy implications. The soft ionic-crystal chemistry is of interest to me, though the discovery is a materials application more than a new molecular concept.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers; Park and Snaith drove solid-state devices and efficiency leaps. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis have substantial claims, so the credit chain is contested.
assessment.maturity: Impact is large but the stability and commercialization question is not settled, which argues for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes pharmacology as induced proximity and has created a new drug modality now in clinical trials. The chemical-biology concept is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli provided structural and VHL-ligand work; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a distinct molecular-glue strand. Compound discovery whose parts may merit different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Approved-drug evidence for PROTACs is not yet established.
PROTACs versus molecular glues may need separate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory gave a physical-chemical solution to Levinthal's paradox and a statistical-mechanical language for folding, binding and function, matched by experimental mapping of folding transition states. It speaks to my physical-chemistry sensibility.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic built the landscape theory; Fersht contributed the experimental phi-value framework; Dill and Bryngelson are also credited. The theory-plus-experiment split could support a configuration.
assessment.maturity: Concept is mature and widely accepted, though the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design may reduce the sense of urgency.
uncertainties: Whether theory or experiment should be primary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single bases without double-strand cleavage, a chemical solution to precise genome editing with therapeutic proof of concept. It is original and carries a clear chemistry perspective.
assessment.attribution: The concept and the first cytosine and adenine base editors came from the Liu lab, so a Liu-only configuration is defensible. Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors; Nishida and Kondo reported a related deaminase approach.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation has begun but remains early; the 2020 CRISPR prize makes a close follow-on recognition possible but not certain.
uncertainties: Timing relative to the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Credit for Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo.
